recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中兩顆中性球的細胞核分成約 6 葉以上、以細絲相連，細胞質顆粒正常；只要看到一顆 ≥6 葉或多顆 5 葉的中性球即屬核分葉過多（hypersegmentation），首先要想到維生素 B12/葉酸缺乏。
features: Two neutrophils with hypersegmented nuclei, each with approximately 6 or more discrete lobes connected by thin chromatin strands
Condensed, clumped mature chromatin within each lobe
Cell size normal to slightly enlarged; cytoplasm pale pink with fine neutrophilic granules, no toxic granulation or vacuoles
Background red cells mostly normocytic with mild anisocytosis; a few platelets present
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows two neutrophils with hypersegmented nuclei, each displaying approximately six or more lobes joined by thin chromatin filaments, with condensed chromatin and normally granulated cytoplasm. No toxic changes or inclusions are present. Background red cells show mild anisocytosis without obvious macro-ovalocytes in this field, and platelets are present. Findings represent neutrophil hypersegmentation, which is suggestive of megaloblastic hematopoiesis (vitamin B12 or folate deficiency) and warrants correlation with MCV and vitamin levels.

ddx.vs: Myelokathectic neutrophils have fewer, rounded, pyknotic lobes separated by very long filaments with chronic neutropenia, rather than many normally shaped lobes.

ddx.dx: Hereditary neutrophil hypersegmentation / drug effect (e.g., hydroxyurea, methotrexate)
ddx.vs: These show similar hypersegmentation; distinction relies on medication history, family studies and normal B12/folate rather than morphology.
Two superimposed band or segmented neutrophils show two cytoplasmic outlines, whereas here each hypersegmented nucleus sits within a single intact cell membrane.
Occasional 5-lobed neutrophils occur in these states, but they lack accompanying macro-ovalocytes and the degree of lobation is usually less marked.
